kashika: तस्मिन्निति सप्तम्यर्थनिर्देशे पूर्वस्यैव कार्यं भवति, नोत्तरस्य। <<इको यणचि>> [[६.१.७७]] — दध्युदकम्। मध्विदम्। पचत्योदनम्। निर्दिष्टग्रहणमानन्तर्यार्थम्। अग्निचिदत्रेति व्यवहितस्य मा भूत्॥
kashikaEnglish: When a rule says 'of that' (तस्मिन्), the operation applies to what precedes.
englishShort: The words in the सप्तमी विभक्ति are used to indicate that the कार्य happens on an immediately previous entity.
englishFull:
A term in the locative case indicates the operation affects what immediately precedes it.

**Example:** @ref[6.1.77] इको यणचि — "यण् replaces इक् when a vowel (अच्) follows."

The locative अचि means the change happens to what precedes the vowel:
दधि + उदकम् → दध्युदकम् (the इ before the following उ becomes य्)

**Why "exhibited" (निर्दिष्ट)?**
The preceding element must be immediately adjacent. In अग्निचित्, the इ of अग्नि is not directly followed by the इ of चित् (intervening च्), so @ref[6.1.77] doesn't apply.
